The intermediate index support for Cauchy–Binet is finite because every sequence vanishes at negative indices. Consecutive minors give the log-concavity of each convolution.

In the conditional comparison a=n−1−v<b=n−1−u, positivity of the right-hand product gives nonnegative a and b, and r(a+1)/r(a)≥r(b+1)/r(b). The zero extension handles the other cases. Expanding the difference of expectations yields the displayed pairing; the pair (0,n) is strictly positive even at n=1. For one positive mean the unique nonzero increment is one. In all cases the increments sum to one.

Shifting the geometric mass by one at fixed values of the other phases gives the stated expectation identity with λ=b/(1+b). Taking the indicator of n produces τ(n−1)p(n−1)−τ(n)p(n)=(n−μ)p(n). Positivity permits division.

The increment of τ is an average of the positive means with all weights strictly positive. Its upper bound b_max is attained exactly when all positive means agree. For n≤μ−b_max, equality of adjacent masses then requires and follows from n=μ−b_max. If μ−b_max<1, the claimed range is empty, including the single-positive-mean case.
